questions.q: What does Parrish say makes areas of competence feel natural and easy?
a: Repeating a task until the mind no longer needs to actively engage
Having natural talent for the activity
Being in a comfortable physical environment
Having strong emotional attachment to the task
questions.why: From the lesson on competences: repeating a task makes the mind stop actively engaging.

questions.q: According to the text, what should you ask yourself after finding the root cause of a problem?
a: Whether fixing it will prevent it from occurring again
How long it will take to implement the fix
Whether others have solved it before
If the problem is worth solving at all
questions.why: From the lesson on root cause: the text says to ask if fixing it prevents recurrence.

questions.q: What type of scenarios does the text say benefit most from thought experiments?
a: Situations where you need to get it right the first time
Tasks that can be repeated many times
Problems with multiple possible solutions
Decisions that involve financial risk
questions.why: From the lesson on long-term thinking: thought experiments work best when you must get it right the first time.

questions.q: What does the text suggest is the result of playing on your strong points?
a: Minimizing the chances of failure
Building new skills over time
Attracting more opportunities
Reducing the need for planning
questions.why: From the lesson on competences: playing on strong points minimizes chances of failure.

questions.q: What does the text say most people do instead of curing the cause of a problem?
a: They try to alleviate its symptoms
They ignore the problem entirely
They blame external factors
They wait for it to resolve itself
questions.why: From the lesson on root cause: most people alleviate symptoms instead of curing the cause.
